newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian soft wheat to fetch A$5/t premium - AWB.
newsitem.headline: Australian soft wheat to fetch A$5/t premium - AWB.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board said on Thursday it has guaranteed soft wheat growers a A$5 a tonne premium to the Australian Standard White 10 percent pool for the 1997/98 harvest.

"Late last year we predicted that this premium may be eroded due to low U.S. Soft White and Western White prices, but with a strengthening in the U.S. market over the past two months and forecasts of a smaller U.S. soft wheat crop in 1998/99, we are confident of achieving our premiums again this harvest," Todd Buck, AWB Soft Wheat Product team leader said in a statement.
Buck said the AWB would continue to use the revised Soft 2 payment scale introduced last year.
"This puts back around A$7 per tonne in the growers' pocket and recognises some of the risks in growing this unique product," Buck said.
Buck also said southern China has emerged as a strong market for Australian soft wheat, with the market growing to 100,000 tonnes in the last five years from nil.
In 1997, the southern China market was likely to surpass South Korea as Australia's biggest buyer of soft wheat, he said.
The export market for soft wheat is growing at a faster rate than increases in production, indicating that demand by 2000 will reach 500,000 tonnes, the AWB said.
